title: I Just Sold a Niche Software Tool for $2.7 Million…Here’s How
promo_conflict: Founder describing his own product and exit.

stated_problem.quote: I had been building a blog for quite a number of years, and the more and more blog posts that you create, the harder it is to find ideas for internal links.
stated_problem.speaker: Spencer Haws

idea.name: Link Whisper: niche WordPress internal-linking plugin (sold for $2.7M)
idea.one_liner: Scratch-your-own-itch SEO plugin filling a feature gap left by big SEO suites, grown via content, email, affiliates, a free WordPress.org version and influencer copies, then sold via broker
idea.customer: bloggers and niche site owners on WordPress
idea.revenue_model: paid licences with freemium WordPress.org version

key_quotes.quote: They had some sort of internal linking reporting, but it was more of like an afterthought, not a full blown out feature.
Anytime I had a customers come in and purchase the product, I had an email series that would go out and invite them to become an affiliate marketer to promote the product to their audience.
And so WordPress.org ended up having 30 to 40,000 free downloads.

claims.quote: I had just sold my niche software company, a WordPress plugin called Link Whisper, for $2.7 million.
And on launch day, it blew my mind because it actually did $30,000 during the launch period, during the very first month.
It actually did about $5,000 to $7,000 in the second and third month.
To eventually, about $90,000 in revenue, on average, each and every month, by the time I sold the company five years later.
I could email 10,000 people that were on my email list that were not customers, and I was guaranteed sales every time I emailed.

acquisition_channels.details: Niche Pursuits list and drip campaigns
customer affiliate invites and influencer free copies

ideas.delivery: WordPress plugin; exit via Quiet Light brokerage with SBA-financed buyer
